## Why

The live URL map serves only `sig-web` — `/v1/*` never reaches
`sig-api`, `/intake/*` is not routed anywhere, the P32.13 nginx's
withdrawal/renamed barriers were never rolled to `sig-web`, and the
API's release registry mount existed nowhere. The contract's shape:
engineer every surface now (IaC, composed analogue, image wiring), prove
the topology in the composed stack, and queue the two hosted legs behind
recorded prestate + byte-compare verification rather than mutating
inside the freeze.

## What ships

- **`ops/lb_routes.toml`** — the committed `sig.lb-routes/1`
  declaration: apex path rules `/v1`+`/v1/*` → `sig-api` (enabled) and
  `/intake`+`/intake/*` → `sig-intake` (`enabled = false` — written,
  never applied live); service→Cloud Run/NEG/backend/composed-upstream
  names for `api`, `web`, `intake`.
- **`ops/src/ops/lb_routes.py` + `sig-ops lb-map
  plan|render|diff|render-edge`** — fail-closed declaration parse;
  `render` merges ONLY the enabled rules onto a live URL-map export
  into the deterministic `url-maps import` document (unowned fields —
  the www→apex redirect, the default service — pass through
  byte-identical); `diff` lists every drift vs the declaration;
  `render-edge` emits the composed edge nginx standing in for the LB.
- **`ops/edge.conf`** — the committed render (drift-checked by test):
  `/v1*` → api, `/intake*` → intake, `/` → web, with Docker-DNS
  `resolver` + variable `proxy_pass` (per-request upstream
  re-resolution) and per-location `proxy_http_version 1.1` (upstream
  gzip needs HTTP/1.1 — both fixes proven live in the composed e2e).
- **`ops/gcp/lb-routes.sh` (L2)** — `--check` plan by default (no ADC,
  no network); `--apply` requires explicit action + ADC + the window
  (exit 42 early/frozen, exit 3 without ADC); actions `prestate`
  (URL-map export + service describes + canonical/run.app
  route-compare baseline), `neg`, `backend`, `urlmap` (renders the
  import FROM the live map + declaration — the disabled intake rule is
  never inserted), `verify` (`lb-map diff` clean + `/v1/health`
  answers the API's JSON-shaped 404 — never the nginx page — since the
  API deliberately has no such route), `rollback` (re-imports the
  recorded prestate, deletes unused resources, refuses a blind
  rollback, stays available outside the mutation window because
  restoring recorded state is safe).
- **`ops/gcp/web-roll.sh` (L1)** — same guard shape over `prestate` →
  `roll` (`ops/gcp/web.sh --apply all`, pinned-digest deploy) →
  `poststate` (revision/digest + zero-diff route-compare on canonical
  + run.app) → `rollback` (new revision at the recorded prior digest —
  never a traffic-only revert).
- **`ops/src/ops/route_compare.py` + `sig-ops route-compare
  capture|verify`** — the dark check: HTTP status + SHA-256 + byte
  length per allow-listed/denied route, before/after each leg; an
  unreachable origin is a hard error, never a diff.
- **`ops/src/ops/web_conf.py` + `sig-ops web-conf`** — deterministic
  `chrome_routes.conf` (`error_page 403 /403.html`, `error_page 410
  /410.html`, exact `/task/` → 404) and `terms_redirect.conf` (real
  302s for `/terms` + `/terms/` — requires `--api-base`, never a
  meta-refresh). Dark by design: the fragments take effect only when
  placed under the site's `conf/` prefix AND nginx rolls/reloads.
- **`ops/web/nginx.conf`** — the `conf/chrome_*.conf` +
  `conf/terms_*.conf` glob includes join the existing
  `withdrawn_*.conf`/`renamed_*.conf` barriers inside the server block;
  `/r/`, `/releases/`, `/entity/`, cache/type protections unchanged.
- **`ops/Dockerfile`** — the api CMD conditionally appends
  `--release-registry /mnt/rel/registry` when the mounted dir exists;
  absent → byte-identical registry-less behaviour (and `uv` pinned to
  the repo's `required-version`, a pre-existing fragility the first
  image build exposed).
- **`ops/docker-compose.yml`** — the `serving` profile: `web` (the real
  `ops/web/Dockerfile` image over `$SIG_SITE_ROOT` → `/mnt/sig-web`),
  `api` (real `ops/Dockerfile` over `$SIG_RELEASE_REGISTRY` →
  `/mnt/rel/registry:ro`), `intake` (`serve-intake`,
  `SIG_INTAKE_ENABLED=1`, `[intake].operational=false` → 503
  `receiver_not_operating`), `edge` (stock nginx + the committed
  `edge.conf`). Benign-default interpolation keeps `sig-ops up/down`
  parseable without the serving vars. Also: `pg_isready -h 127.0.0.1`
  in the db healthcheck — the socket-only check reported healthy during
  initdb and released sqitch into a refused TCP connect.
- **API release-search links** — the HTML surface's `href`/`action`
  attributes are pinned root-absolute or fully absolute (never
  relative, never loopback-bound) by a new invariant test.

## Boundaries

No production mutation ran and none may run inside the freeze: no
`gcloud --apply`/`import`/`deploy`, no NEG/backend/URL-map write, no
service roll — only the read-only describes/exports committed as
prestate evidence. `/intake/*` renders nowhere live (`enabled = false`;
P37.59 owns the receiver service; `D-P32.16-1` keeps it
non-operational). The generated chrome/terms fragments are NOT placed
under any bucket `conf/` — `D-P34.13-1` stays OPEN (its verify reads
"after the roll"). The registry mount is engineered, not rolled —
P34.46/P35.53/P35.57 own the registry bucket + api roll. No
`ingestion_permitted` flip, no `HG-nn` tick, no spine UPDATE/DELETE, no
CI config change, no living-record assertion.
